definitions_and_conventions: A cell average is the integral of q over a grid cell divided by the volume of that cell.
A Riemann problem consists of the hyperbolic equation together with piecewise-constant initial data having one jump at x=0.
The Riemann convention is q_l for x<0 and q_r for x>0.
In the surrounding finite-volume description, a numerical flux is intended to approximate the correct flux using the approximate cell averages available.
implicit_context: The finite-volume quantities being supplied as Riemann states are cell averages rather than pointwise values.
The assignment is oriented: the i-1 cell supplies the left state and the i cell supplies the right state.
The phrase “can be used” states an operational role for the Riemann information; it does not identify that information with a unique flux value or update formula.
